rules.rule: **The game draws a Bedrock model mirrored in x.** A cube's `"east"` UV is shown on its LOW-x side, `"west"` on its high-x side, and across every face the texture runs the other way from the naive reading. `data/face-mapping.json` is the table. A renderer that ignores this lies to you.
**A JSON rotation `[rx, ry, rz]` is applied as right-handed `(-rx, ry, -rz)`, X then Y then Z.** Animation rotations are **added** to the bone's bind rotation.

**No stair steps.** Slopes and curves are tilted boxes joined corner to corner. Where a width steps, splay a box out to the wider corner. Fill valley joints by running both links past the corner. A tilted part's end runs INTO what it meets.
**No two faces on one plane.** Move one part 0.02–0.05. Then **paint the thin step that appears so it continues its neighbour** — unpainted steps look like cracks.
**The design flows as one piece.** A motif stuck on the front "looks like a lizard". Do not reuse another model's front or sides.
**A body is closed.** Its face must not show its own sides; nothing floats; no inside is visible from where the player looks (a wheel from the seat, a hollow neck from below).
**One silhouette, one balance.** If one end is raised, raise the rest: balance is judged on the whole side view.
**Nothing fixed may stand in a moving part's path**, in any pose. Model the part open; fold it with the bind pose; check folded, half, open and overshoot.
**One bone per thing that moves**, pivot at the real joint; pieces that read as one share ONE pivot.

**A membrane, fin, leaf, cloth or grille is ONE zero-thickness plate whose outline is cut by transparent texels** (material `entity_alphatest`) — the way the vanilla Ender Dragon makes its wings — not a board and not a fan of boxes. Its two faces lie in one plane and are both drawn: paint them **by position** so they agree at every point. When vanilla has the thing you are making, **open the vanilla pack and look first**.
**Texture nobody can see must go (one texel); texture meant to be seen must be visible.** Check visibility from every direction, in every pose. Bones that an animation moves freely are exempt.
**Pictures that cross cubes are placed by position**, not by texel index, so lines run on from one cube to the next.
**Fit what the model touches**: the seated rider, the hand that holds it, the head that wears it. Test against the pose the game really shows.

**When a human hand-edits the model, their file wins.** Deploy it as is; fix only real defects (say which); bring the builder to THEIR geometry. Fix what they point at — a redesign of the whole part gets rejected.

**Look at it.** Render after every change, from the camera the player will have, in every pose, in a light and a dark livery. "The checks pass" is not "it looks right". Never report a look you have not rendered.
**Heavy loops do not belong in Python.** Rasterising visibility in Node took a build from 150 s to 24 s.
**Physics footprints are measured**, from the rest-pose corners of the structural bones — never eyeballed.
